text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The paper's editorial says the government is responsible for the get-rich-quick pyramid schemes, one of which has collapsed with 30,000 people having invested $13 million. Another has declared temporary suspension of its activities.

- Experts say the former head of the National Information Service Irakli Kocollari and the deputy interior minister Vladimir Hysi ordered that no collaborators' files be burned. They are being tried on charges they ordered their destruction.
- Panic erupted and police were called in after hundreds of people demanded their money back after Sude, which allegedly runs a pyramid scheme, said it would halt all activities until December 18.
- The International Monetary Fund said the pyramid schemes were a matter for the government to sort out.
- An international fair failed to open on schedule after the goods to be exhibited did not clear customs on time.
- Police have arrested five associates of Aleksander Grunjasi, the operator of a collapsed $13 million pyramid scheme, after many of its 30,000 creditors filed lawsuits.
- Albania has begun taking the first steps towards privatisation of the health system, a process expected to end in 10 years.

- The centrist partnership between the centre-right Democratic Alliance and the centre-left Social Democratic Party will form a new alliance called the Freedom Pole which would also include the Democratic Party of the Right.
- Albanian Finance Minister Ridvan Bode says the responsibility for the viability of alleged pyramid money schemes is a matter for the private persons who run them.
- French President Jacques Chirac has invited Albanian President Sali Berisha to France.
- Albania's budget deficit has swollen to 26 billion leks ($26 million).
